tasks.task: Write a design document for a new system or major change

items.when: When a new product, service or major change is about to be built and needs the full run
When goals are clear and you need scenarios, diagrams, key flows and trade-offs in one doc
Before you settle, to see an architecture choice set against its alternatives and trade-offs
When the core is a backend, to get a right-sized setup, tables, an API outline and a failure plan
When the draft is done, to have reviewers test it in turn for hidden assumptions
Before sign-off, to list the ways the design could fail and the changes that avoid them
When the design covers only the happy path and not errors, overload or bad handoffs

tasks.task: Review a current or proposed architecture

items.when: When a system must be checked against its quality goals and the cloud provider's pillars
When the system runs on AWS, to list gaps and fixes against AWS workload guidance
When the system runs on Azure, to list gaps and fixes against Azure workload guidance
When you can read the code, to find design problems the diagrams do not show
When outages are the worry, to find missing timeouts, retries and circuit breakers

tasks.task: Write a decision record for a big technical choice

items.when: When a choice is made or due, to record context, options, the decision and its consequences
When the options are named, to compare cost, security, team fit and long-term support
When one unknown blocks the decision, to plan a short study with an owner and a deadline
When a small choice needs only a short note of why and what was passed over
When the team is stuck, to ask if the choice can be undone cheaply and decide at that speed

tasks.task: Run a design-level threat model

items.when: When a system or feature needs a data flow diagram, trust boundaries and a threat pass
When you want a second pass that rates each threat by risk with a way to reduce it
When sensitive data is involved, to trace its paths and what a breach would expose
When an API or config design is new, to find the parts that are easy to misuse
When the model must end in a list of proposed controls for each trust boundary
When a control is proposed, to ask what it protects, what it costs and what risk remains

tasks.task: Draw context, container and flow diagrams

items.when: When you need a shared picture of a system from a description, folder list or resource list
When a flow, sequence or database diagram must paste straight into the docs
When the picture is for a slide or a client and should be a finished image, not code
When the diagrams are drawn, to test whether they match the design and hide no assumption

tasks.task: Turn vague requirements into measurable quality scenarios

items.when: When someone says fast, scalable, secure or reliable and you need numbers first
When reliability needs a target users would feel, an error budget and alert rules
When scale needs numbers, to link traffic, tested limits and running cost

tasks.task: Choose a tech stack, database or vendor with trade-offs

items.when: When two or three stacks are in play, to compare them side by side and get a pick
When the question is which database, to get a pick, a schema and a safe migration plan
When the data is large or spread out, to choose storage, copies, splitting and consistency
When buying is an option, to score vendors against your criteria with risk notes
When the choice is made, to write down why so the next person understands

tasks.task: Decide between a monolith, modular monolith or services

items.when: When the team debates splitting a system or starting a product as microservices
When you want each shape drawn with its trade-offs before you argue for one
When the split is assumed, to question the requirement and delete parts before adding any
When a shape is chosen, to stress it for ways the split could fail the team

tasks.task: Choose a multi-tenancy model for a SaaS product

items.when: When a product serves many customers and you must decide what is shared and what is separate
When tenant data size differs a lot, to plan how to split and copy the data
When tenants need single sign-on and roles, to design login, sessions and permissions
When the model is chosen, to check one tenant cannot reach another's data

tasks.task: Outline the data model and the API

items.when: When the app is described, to get tables, links, indexes and rules in a clean schema
When the service needs routes, status codes, paging and docs planned
When partners will call the API, to set contract rules, versioning and rate limits
When an API spec exists, to score it and flag breaking changes and naming problems

tasks.task: Review a cloud bill and find the waste

items.when: When the cloud bill keeps growing or nobody can explain the main costs
When the bill is AWS, to weigh each saving against the risk to the workload
When the bill is Azure, to get a resource map, price estimates and a savings plan
When you have access to the AWS account, to list idle resources and the saving for each
After the review, to track what grew each month and the caps to add
When each cost has a defender, to ask what the requirement behind it really is

tasks.task: Design the cloud set-up on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud

items.when: When AWS is a candidate, to get a design with serverless parts, templates and cost cuts
When Azure is a candidate, to get a design with templates, a pipeline and cost cuts
When Google Cloud is a candidate, to get services, a cost estimate and deploy steps
When the provider is chosen, to write the set-up down with diagrams and trade-offs
When set-up files exist, to find open buckets and loose access rules

tasks.task: Write Terraform for the chosen cloud set-up

items.when: When the design is agreed, to get Terraform modules with safe state and clean structure
When the team uses Pulumi or CloudFormation, not Terraform
Before anything is applied, to check the files for loose access and open storage

tasks.task: Plan a move to a new host, cloud or data store

items.when: When the move must not take the system down, to plan checks and a rollback per step
When an old system is being retired, to move users over without breaking them
Before the move, to record why the new home was chosen over staying put
When the plan is drafted, to list how the cutover could fail and what avoids it
When the move changes behaviour that users or other systems rely on today

tasks.task: Set reliability targets and a recovery plan

items.when: When nobody has said how reliable the service must be, to set targets and an error budget
When you must state how much loss is acceptable and plan backups and a restore drill
When backups exist but a restore was never tested, to plan the test and log the proof
When the design claims to survive a failure, to plan a safe experiment that proves it
When the plan lists failures but not which job wins when several hit at once

tasks.task: Plan monitoring, alerts and runbooks

items.when: When a service has no clear signals, to plan metrics, logs, traces and alerts step by step
When the design is live, to write runbooks for deploy, incidents and rollback
First, to name the numbers the alerts should protect

tasks.task: Run the quarterly architecture health check

items.when: Every three months, and after any major incident
When the check shows drift from the quality goals and one area needs a closer look
When you need the debt that slows the team ranked, with cost and small fixes
Between checks, to find new debt each month and confirm the last clean-up
Between checks, to track new, open and fixed package risks and an upgrade order
After a major incident, to turn the timeline into a report and tracked prevention actions

tasks.task: Design login, single sign-on and permissions

items.when: When the app needs login, single sign-on, session rules and account recovery designed
When a login and permissions plan exists and needs a review
When the design is drafted, to test each sign-in path for spoofing and privilege gain

tasks.task: Design an AI feature, retrieval set-up or agent system

items.when: First, to decide between a model API and fine-tuning, with a cost break-even
When answers must come from the client's documents, to choose chunking, embeddings and a store
When several agents are planned, to compare supervisor, swarm and handoff designs
When the design is drafted, to see where tokens go and cut the bill without hurting quality
When the AI reads outside text, to map and block hidden instructions

tasks.task: Design a data pipeline or reporting store

items.when: When reports need raw, cleaned and report-ready layers with quality checks and alerts
When you must choose where the data lives and how consistent it must be
When the pipeline is a major change and needs flows and trade-offs written down

tasks.task: Design how systems talk to each other

items.when: First, to draw which systems call which and where the data crosses a boundary
When two teams or vendors share an API, to catch breaking changes before they ship
When a call to another system can hang or fail, to plan timeouts, retries and fallbacks
When the interface is drafted, to find the parts a caller could misuse

tasks.task: Shape the design for an audit or privacy rules

items.when: When a customer asks for SOC 2, to map controls, gaps and the evidence an auditor wants
When personal data is stored, to map where it lives and make deletion reach every system
When the design leans on a vendor for sensitive data, to tier the risk and set questions

tasks.task: Decide whether to rewrite, refactor or retire an old system

items.when: Before deciding, to rank the debt that slows the team and see what each fix would cost
When a part seems too rotten to patch, to justify a rebuild and keep what worked
When the old system is retired, to plan moving users without breaking them
When the call is made, to record the options and why this one won

tasks.task: Advise a founder on team, stack and build order

items.when: When a founder needs a view on tech debt, hiring and the next architecture calls
When the founder is choosing a stack before the first hire
When a one-server set-up is starting to strain and the founder asks what to change first

always.when: Before any design or plan goes out, to list how it could fail
Whenever a choice is made in passing, to leave a short note of why

helpers.when: When the design needs pipelines, containers or infrastructure code built and run
When the threat model finds risks that need code-level review and fixes
When the schema, indexes or a data migration need detailed design and tuning
When the API and services in the design must be built or prototyped
When the design includes pipelines and a warehouse that someone must build
When an AI feature in the design needs prompts, evaluation and model choice worked out

gaps: No library item draws C4 context and container diagrams; the library only has general diagram makers
No library item turns words like fast, scalable or secure into measurable quality scenarios
No library item decides between a monolith, a modular monolith and services
No library item chooses a multi-tenancy model or checks tenant isolation
No library item reviews a Google Cloud set-up or bill; the reviews cover AWS and Azure only
No library item plans a move from one host or cloud to another; only a general zero-downtime plan exists
No library item designs queues, events or caching, or says when each is worth adding
No library item checks that a diagram matches the system it claims to show
No thinking lens in the library covers distributed systems or software architecture
No library item picks a region or data location for common markets; only UAE and Saudi rules are covered
